explanations.explanation: A colt, friend. Jesus says they'll find one tied there as soon as they enter the village (Mark 11:2). He gives the whole plan before they take a single step. I'd have forgotten what I was sent for by the second street.
A camel would be a LOT of animal, friend. Jesus says they'll find a colt tied there (Mark 11:2). That's the one on the errand list. A camel on this errand would be quite the surprise.

A ram, friend? That would make for a pushy errand. Jesus says they'll find a colt tied there as soon as they enter the village (Mark 11:2). A colt is what He names, so a colt is what they go looking for.
True, friend. Jesus calls it a colt "…on which no one has ever sat." (Mark 11:2) A colt with no riding miles on it at all. I know a thing or two about being well used, and this colt is the opposite.

Not quite, baker, and I'd say that was a sneaky one. Jesus does say it, in His own words: a colt "…on which no one has ever sat." (Mark 11:2) So the statement is true. Jesus knows this colt well enough to tell the two disciples exactly where to find it and how to get it, and that's a lot of detail to hand out before the colt has even been untied.

explanations.answer: The Lord needs it and will return it shortly
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus tells them to say, "The Lord needs it and will return it shortly." (Mark 11:3) Short, clear, and it even says the colt is coming back. I wish my instructions came that tidy. Mine usually end with "you'll figure it out."

explanations.answer: The Teacher will pay you back for it tonight
explanations.explanation: Good thinking, baker, but that's not the line. Jesus tells them to say, "The Lord needs it and will return it shortly." (Mark 11:3) Paying somebody back is a different thing from returning the colt. And nothing about tonight. The words He hands them are the words they use.

explanations.answer: The priests have sent us here to collect it
explanations.explanation: No priests in this errand, friend. Jesus tells the two disciples to say, "The Lord needs it and will return it shortly." (Mark 11:3) The words come from Jesus, and they're short enough to remember while your heart is pounding.

Not this time, baker. The text says the disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, "…and the people gave them permission." (Mark 11:6). Nobody blocks the way. Jesus handed them the right words, and they worked.

False is right, friend. The disciples answer as Jesus instructed, and "…the people gave them permission." (Mark 11:6) No standoff, no arguing. I bet those two let out a breath they'd been holding the whole walk.

True, baker. The disciples lead the colt to Jesus, throw their cloaks over it, "…and He sat on it." (Mark 11:7) The colt nobody had ridden before now has Jesus on it. The errand worked out just as He said.

Not false, friend. The text says they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, "…and He sat on it." (Mark 11:7) The colt that no one had ever sat on now has Jesus on it. So the answer is True.

Branches, baker! Others in the crowd spread "…branches they had cut from the fields." (Mark 11:8) Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread the branches. Cloaks and branches, all laid down on the road.

Grain sounds like a field thing, I'll give you that. But the text says others spread "…branches they had cut from the fields." (Mark 11:8) Grain isn't what Mark names. Branches are the answer, and many also spread their cloaks on the road.
Straw is a good field guess, friend. But Mark says others spread "…branches they had cut from the fields." (Mark 11:8) Straw isn't mentioned. Many also spread their cloaks on the road.

David, baker! The crowd shouts, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) David was made king over Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), and the crowd calls him "our father." The ones who went ahead and those who followed were all shouting.
Abraham is a big name, friend, but he's not the one in this shout. The crowd shouts, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) The kingdom they name is David's.

Jacob is a good guess, baker, but he's not the name in this shout. The crowd cries, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) David was made king over Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), and it's his kingdom they bless.
True, baker. Jesus entered Jerusalem "…and went into the temple courts." (Mark 11:11) After the shouting on the road, that's where He goes. And there He looks around at everything.
Not false, friend. Mark says Jesus entered Jerusalem "…and went into the temple courts." (Mark 11:11) The crowd was LOUD, and then He goes right in. That's where the next part happens.

explanations.answer: Goes out to Bethany with the Twelve
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Since it was already late, Jesus "…went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) He looks around at everything first, and then He heads out. And the story isn't over yet.

explanations.answer: Stays the night in the temple courts
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says that since it was already late, Jesus "…went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) He heads out of the temple courts instead of staying. And the story isn't over yet.

explanations.answer: Heads back to Jericho with the crowd
explanations.explanation: Jericho isn't in this verse, baker. Mark says that since it was already late, Jesus "…went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) Bethany is where He heads, and the Twelve are who the text names as going with Him. And the story isn't over yet.
